title: Direct matrix swaps through canonical storage
objective: Replace whole-matrix-copy row and column swaps with checked O(n)/O(m) direct mutation for canonical ZZ, QQ, packed small GF(p), and M4RI GF(2) matrices; preserve Sage semantics and prove backend selection and scaling.

oracles: Existing matrix selection implementation as differential oracle
exceptions: Thin host-neutral inline adapters unwrap generated owned resources to mature FLINT/M4RI swap primitives; packed GF(p) remains source-transparent typed Python and no handwritten mathematical algorithm or N-API callback is added.

handoff.summary: Added checked generated FLINT and M4RI row/column swap declarations, host-neutral adapters, source-transparent packed GF(p) kernels, and public in-place routing with cache invalidation and preserved resource identity. Native and disabled-native behavior agree across ZZ, QQ, GF(2), and GF(97). Warm 100-swap measurements on 1000x1000 matrices were 8.25/8.52 ms for ZZ rows/columns, 23.01/10.03 ms for QQ, 8.73/8.00 ms for GF(2), and 8.16/10.03 ms for GF(97); a single direct row swap was 19x to 143x faster than the superseded whole-matrix selection strategy. The generated adapter growth raised the measured native-integration lazy footprint by 7826 bytes, so its ratchet moved minimally from 600000 to 605000 bytes.
risks: The full validated run was linux-x64; macOS ARM64 and browser/WASM should exercise the same declared symbols during integration before release.

The broad changed-file suite hit one pre-existing timing-sensitive uint64 packing ratio assertion under concurrent load; its immediate isolated rerun passed (1.49 ms for 500x500 versus 0.85 ms small).
next_steps: Review generated declaration identity churn and the public no-copy/storage-identity assertions before cherry-picking.
Run the focused swap test and benchmark on the M1 portability host after integration.
